subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency targets (Finly)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Li <ethan.li@finly.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency targets (Finly)

Hi Ethan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciate the context and time. Below is a short recap of what we heard, success criteria you called out, and next steps we discussed. Please flag anything I missed or mis-stated.

What we heard (pain points)
- UI streaming stalls at the p95 for chat: users see noticeable pauses during generation (esp. with 3+ concurrent edits).
- Current stack: self-hosted open models (custom batching on k8s), front-end expects streaming chunks for progressive rendering.
- Peak concurrency: ~150-200 concurrent live chat sessions during peak; sustained concurrency ~80-120.
- Cost sensitivity: token costs and instance-hours are primary gating factors for a PoC.

Success criteria (what Finly would call “win”)
- p95 latency for streaming chunks (first token and steady-state streaming) < 300ms for typical 256-token responses.
- UI shouldn’t stall (no >1s stalls) during any 95th percentile slot under target concurrency.
- Sustained concurrency support of 150 req/s with headroom for 200 burst.
- Deterministic token ordering and low jitter for streaming so front-end can safely stitch partial responses.

Technical notes / constraints
- Must integrate with your existing auth and audit stack (SAML + internal KMS).
- Prefers quantized models to reduce memory footprint; open to Redwood’s recommended model variants.
- Streaming API must support chunked response with token-level timestamps (or stable chunk boundaries).

Attachments
- redwood-discovery-March2026.pdf (high-level approach and example PoC plan)

Next steps (agreed)
1) Finly to share recent load test results and a short sample of typical requests (+ front-end expectations) — Ethan to send by Mon (29 Feb).
2) Set up a technical deep-dive: Aditya + Dev + Marissa + Finly engs to go over inference profile and batching strategy (target week of Mar 2).
3) Redwood to propose a PoC plan and success metrics (3-4 week PoC) after reviewing load tests.
4) Quick pricing/elasticity note: if we can meet the p95 target with quantized variants, we’ll include a cost estimate for both Hosted and Dedicated options.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed slots for the technical deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency targets (Finly)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — this is spot on. A few clarifications and the load test attached.

Clarifications from our side:
- The UI streaming "stall" is most noticeable on first-token latency for longer contexts (>512 tokens) and when multiple concurrent users trigger generation at the same time (e.g., bulk import + live edits).
- Our current 95th percentile numbers (from last week’s run): first-token p95 = ~880ms, steady-state token p95 = ~420ms under a ~120 concurrent workload.
- Peak burst we need to plan for is 200 concurrent, but steady-state target is 150.
- We can provide a small redacted dataset of typical requests and a lightweight front-end integration test harness.

Attached: finly-load-test-20260226.csv (load test summary + raw samples)

Timeline: we’re targeting a PoC kickoff the week of Mar 9; happy to slide if you need more time for prep.

Thanks,
Ethan
VP Product, Finly

Ethan — perfect, thanks for the numbers and the CSV. That helps a lot. Proposed next steps from Redwood: 

1) Technical deep-dive (60m) — proposed attendees: Aditya (serving/runtime), Dev (infra & deployment), Dylan (integration/SDK).
   - Agenda: review load test trace, discuss batching/kv-cache strategy, streaming chunking semantics, and potential model variants to meet <300ms p95.
2) PoC plan (3-4 weeks) — baseline + tuned run: we’ll run a small PoC using a quantized model variant and adjust batching/streaming settings. Key success metrics will be the p95 targets and UI stall reduction.
3) Pre-PoC ask: Finly to provide a short sample of 50 representative requests + a front-end harness (or recording) so we can validate streaming UX.
4) Cost estimate: we’ll prepare Hosted vs Dedicated estimates after the deep-dive and initial PoC sizing.

- Wed Mar 3, 10:00—11:00
- Thu Mar 4, 14:00—15:00
